sentences.text: This small dinosaur measured about two meters in length and weighed approximately twenty kilograms.
The holotype specimen — the specific fossil the species is based on — includes two lower legs with tibiotarsi, metatarsi, and toes from the Nemegt Formation.
The tibiotarsi of this animal have an estimated length of twenty-eight centimetres.
Its anatomy features a very elongated tibiotarsus, a narrow third toe, and a short, relatively flat claw on the second toe.
Osmólska suggested that the second toe regained a weight-bearing function to compensate for the weakness of the third toe.
Osmólska assigned Borogovia to the family Troodontidae in 1987, noting it might be a junior synonym of Saurornithoides.
A 2021 study recovered Borogovia as a member of the subfamily Troodontinae, closely related to Saurornithoides.
However, a 2021 revision by Cau and Madzia recovered Borogovia as a sister taxon to the subfamily Troodontinae.
Borogovia lived approximately 70 million years ago during the Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous Period in what is now Mongolia.
Researchers have suggested that Borogovia, Saurornithoides, and Tochisaurus found at the same site might be the same species.
